Code and data behind my studies are released on [GitHub](https://github.com/fatihbozdag) and the [Open Science Framework](https://osf.io/vz746/) where copyright allows. Everything below is Python unless stated otherwise.

## Main tools

::: {.tool .featured}
### bitig
[Computational stylometry]{.kicker}

Authorship attribution, author-group style comparison and forensic authorship analysis: Delta, Zeta, PCA/MDS, clustering, bootstrap consensus trees and classification (the core of R's *Stylo*), plus a spaCy pipeline, transformer embeddings, a Bayesian layer (PyMC) and likelihood-ratio–calibrated authorship verification. Supports EN, TR, DE, ES, FR. Named after the Old Turkic word for *inscription*.
[Documentation](https://fatihbozdag.github.io/bitig/) · [GitHub](https://github.com/fatihbozdag/bitig) · [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/bitig/)
[BSD-3-Clause]{.meta}
:::

::: {.tool .featured}
### Linguistic Clusters Framework
[Distributional stability in learner constructions]{.kicker}

Pipeline for identifying stable distributional patterns in learner English passives: instance-level association measures (transitional probability, ΔP, boundary entropy), schema acceptance via NPMI or slot entropy, and validation by permutation, sensitivity and ablation analysis. Replication material for the *Corpus Linguistics and Linguistic Theory* (2026) article.
[GitHub](https://github.com/fatihbozdag/linguistic_clusters) · [OSF](https://osf.io/kq7gv/)
:::

::: {.tool .featured}
### Metalinguistics
[Metadiscourse analysis]{.kicker}

Detection and classification of metadiscourse markers in academic text (Hyland's eight categories) with a transformer-based spaCy pipeline and a feature-based classifier; distinguishes academic from conversational uses. Used in the *Journal of Language Research* (2025) study on Turkish EFL metadiscourse.
[GitHub](https://github.com/fatihbozdag/metadiscourse_analysis)
[MIT]{.meta}
:::

::: {.tool .featured}
### Statistical Methods in Learner Corpus Research
[Interactive companion]{.kicker}

Fourteen lessons on the statistical methods behind my studies, from rates and their denominators to hierarchical Bayesian models, cross-fitting and the provenance of reported numbers. Each lesson explains one method, lets the reader test it on an invented example in an interactive diagram, and shows where the method appears in the papers.
[Open the companion](stats/)
:::

## Research code

Smaller repositories that accompany individual studies.

::: {.tool}
### PassivePy
[Passive voice detection]{.kicker}

Passive construction detection and pattern analysis, with comparison of detection methods and visualisation.
[GitHub](https://github.com/fatihbozdag/passive_detection)
:::

::: {.tool}
### Tense annotation tool
[Learner-text annotation]{.kicker}

Web application for annotating English tense–aspect structures in learner texts by CEFR level: role-based access, categorised tense options with instructions, auto-save, progress tracking and CSV export.
[GitHub](https://github.com/fatihbozdag/annotator)
:::

::: {.tool}
### Grammar research with spaCy
[Study pipelines]{.kicker}

Collection of reproducible pipelines for grammar analysis in learner English, each module tied to a published study, among them the dative-alternation analysis behind the *TAPSLA* (2024) article.
[GitHub](https://github.com/fatihbozdag/Grammar-Research-with-Spacy)
:::

::: {.tool}
### Lexical complexity across CEFR levels
[Replication code]{.kicker}

Code base for Bozdağ & Kilimci (2024), *Lexical complexity and language proficiency: An investigation of indices across CEFR levels*.
[GitHub](https://github.com/fatihbozdag/lexical_complexity)
:::

## Corpora I work with

ICLE (International Corpus of Learner English, incl. the Turkish sub-corpus TICLE), EFCAMDAT, PELIC and the Turkish National Corpus. I do not redistribute licensed corpus data; scripts expect the user's own copy.
